To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transfection properties of DNA/PEI complexes are improved when the excess of polymer is removed.
the purification of crude PEI/DNA complexes, which is achieved by centrifugation-based size-exclusion ultrafiltration, improves their in vitro and in vivo performances.
the purification of PEI/DNAs leads to more efficient gene transfer in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient and less toxic polyplexes, and the purification of polyplexes from the excess of polymer.
the development of a new generation of PEI/DNAs complexes, with a better balance between transfection efficacy and toxicity.
the optimization of PEI-based polyplexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the purification process is essential for the preparation of efficient and safe PEI/DNA complexes.
the use of genuine DNA–PEI polyplexes is a key step to improve transfection properties and cell survival.
the use of a purification assay, based on ultrafiltration of crude polyplexes, leads to a more efficient and less toxic gene transfer system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PEGylation of pre-formed PEI polyplexes leads not only to a reduction in the toxicity of the polycomplex but also to an increase in transfection efficiency.
PEGylation of PEI/DNAA polyplexes should be performed after complexation, and purification of the crude polyplexes is required.
the use of purified polyplexes is highly recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PEI/DNA complexes are not inert and that purification of the crude complexes is a key step to achieve efficient and non-toxic gene delivery.
PEI/DNA complexes should be purified from free PEI, in order to achieve efficient and safe gene delivery.
the use of purified PEI/DNA complexes is a simple way to improve the efficiency of in vivo gene transfer.
